objectives: Hear and identify /b/ in spoken words.
Identify /b/ at the beginning and end of taught-pattern words.
Discriminate /b/ from similar taught consonants, especially /p/.
Prepare for b grapheme mapping and CVC decoding.
concepts: Phoneme identity can be recognised without print.
A consonant sound can occur in different word positions.
Minimal sound contrasts support accurate phoneme discrimination.
Reliable auditory recognition precedes efficient grapheme mapping.

definitions.definition: The smallest unit of sound in a spoken word.
The first phoneme heard in a word.
The last phoneme heard in a word.

workedExamples: Contrast bat and pat to hear /b/ versus /p/.
commonMistakes: Hearing only the first sound and ignoring final /b/.
Using letter names instead of speech sounds.
Guessing from word meaning rather than listening.
keyTakeaways: Map b to /b/ after auditory mastery.

application: Identify the correct grapheme for an heard /b/ sound.
higherOrderThinking: Explain how word position changes where /b/ is heard.
mixedReview: Mix /b/ with previously taught consonants for auditory discrimination.

formulaOrFactBank: b represents /b/ in the taught phonics sequence.
mistakeBasedRevision: If /b/ is confused with /p/, listen to the initial phoneme again and compare the contrast pair.
weakTopicRevision: Use fresh spoken /b/ words in initial and final positions.

activities.name: /b/ contrast
steps: Say a /b/ word and a /p/ word.

outcomes: Learner reliably identifies /b/ in spoken words.
Learner recognises /b/ in initial and final positions and is ready for grapheme mapping.

questions.question: Which pair begins with different sounds?

It makes all CVC words identical.

questions.question: What should come after reliable /b/ sound identification?
options: Map b to /b/ in print and begin decoding.
Move immediately to long multisyllabic words.
